scope: Public sources for a representative 200 mm plasma-assisted GaN chamber and for published simulation-versus-measurement test cases per subsystem. sources.title: Dissociation energies of the Ga2, In2, and GaIn molecules

Measurement uncertainty (+/-2 K) is comparable to the +/-3 K non-uniformity, limiting discrimination between models. GaAs substrate, not GaN-on-Si; 983 K target, below GaN growth temperatures. sources.title: A detailed study of the molecular beam flux distribution of MBE effusion sources
sources.supports: Bismuth from graphite crucibles, cylindrical and conical (taper 2.6 deg), aperture D = 16.5 mm; quartz-microbalance scan across +/-48 mm in a plane normal to the crucible axis at R = 115 mm (one case 265 mm). Measured: filling level L/D (Fig. 3), source temperature / rate (Figs. 2, 4), 60 deg inclination at 0.07 and 26.5 A/s (Fig. 5), cylindrical vs conical at L/D = 2 (Fig. 6), 115 vs 265 mm at L/D = 2, 593 C, centre rates 10.0 and 1.9 A/s (Fig. 7). Findings: central ~30 mm plateau independent of L/D, strong fill-level effect outside it; higher rate flattens the profile; inclination effect small up to 60 deg; 1/R^2 holds; intermolecular collisions in the crucible matter above ~0.2 A/s (Knudsen number lambda/D < 12), so collisionless crucible models fail at practical rates. Transfer method to a rotating substrate with a virtual point source at the taper apex; example for VG V80H geometry q = 160 mm, h = 302 mm, 24 deg (Fig. 9).

Distance scan at 46 deg: range below 1.4 % beyond 300 mm. Shapes at 40 deg / 350 mm: cylindrical 4.36 %, conical 1.4 %, constricted-neck 2.35 %. Flux falls about linearly with source consumption (slope about -2/3 at centre). Also lists 8-inch-class tools: RIBER MBE8000 (4x8-inch), Veeco GEN2000 (7x6-inch), CETC 48 (4x6-inch).
sources.does_not_support: Measurement: simulation only, so agreement is code-to-code corroboration, not validation. Non-uniformity metric is not defined and does not reproduce exactly from Fig. 10; depth 174 vs 170 mm inconsistency; distance used in the angle scan not stated explicitly (Table 1 gives 350 mm). CdTe, not Ga/Al.
sources.use: Code-to-code comparison for the crucible emission model on an 8-inch geometry: optimum angle near 46 deg, base-case centre-to-edge ratio about 0.90, crucible-shape ranking.

sources.title: Simultaneously monitoring Ga adsorption and desorption kinetics on GaN(0001) using four in situ techniques
sources.authors: H. Zhang, P. John, J. Kang, L. Geelhaar, Y. Cho, O. Brandt (Paul-Drude-Institut)
sources.source_locator: Sec. II (setup, flux calibration), Eqs. 1-8, Fig. 2-3, Table S1
sources.supports: Ga adlayer desorption on GaN(0001) without N: rate constant gamma 0.118 / 0.068 / 0.04 s^-1 at 708 / 693 / 676 C (maximum adlayer coverage 2.4 ML), activation energy 2.87 +/- 0.04 eV from four techniques (RHEED, laser reflectometry, line-of-sight QMS, pyrometry). Maximum adlayer desorption flux 0.28 ML/s at 708 C. Ga flux: absolute to 5 % (SEM thickness of N-rich layers), relative to better than 2 % (retractable ion gauge BEP vs cell temperature). Pyrometer artefacts on GaN: reflected Ga-cell radiation shifts the reading by about 0.5 C at shutter operation; cell radiation heats the wafer; the Ga adlayer changes emissivity (Eq. 5-8). Laser reflectometry (650 nm) responds to adlayer and droplets.
sources.does_not_support: Droplet onset during growth under N flux (no N during the transients); absolute substrate temperature (pyrometer on a Ti-coated back side, assumed emissivity 0.55); 200 mm wafers; reproducibility over campaigns.
sources.use: Fourth droplet-onset scenario candidate (prefactor 1.6e14 ML/s, 2.87 eV; matches the Ref14 slope, lies between Heying and Ref14 at 708 C); evidence for the 2 % BFM relative-flux prior; pyrometer error terms for the reading budget.
sources.follow_up: See ref/notes/RESEARCH_GAP_SEARCH_2026-10-06.md for how each source bears on the twin.

sources.title: In situ measurements of wafer bending curvature during growth of group-III-nitride layers on silicon by molecular beam epitaxy
sources.authors: Y. Cordier, N. Baron, F. Semond, J. Massies, M. Binetti et al. (CRHEA)
sources.source_locator: Sec. 2-3; Fig. 1; Table 1
sources.supports: CRHEA, Riber Compact 21 (NH3 MBE), 50 mm Si(111), LayTec EpiCurve + EpiTT: radiatively heated wafers do not change temperature with bending, even at curvatures near 0.3 m^-1 (unlike MOCVD). In-growth curvature reaches -0.24 to -0.31 m^-1 (convex, compressive) and changes by about 0.2 m^-1 on cooling. A plain IR pyrometer (0.91-0.97 um) shows +/-20 C oscillations from GaN thin-film interference and about 20 C absolute difference from the emissivity-corrected EpiTT reading; the corrected optical head reduces parasitic radiation from the hot sources to about 2 K.
sources.does_not_support: 200 mm wafers or plasma-source growth (this paper is ammonia MBE); the size of view-factor changes at larger bow.
sources.use: Supports neglecting bow in the radiative heater model; at 0.3 m^-1 a 200 mm wafer sags about 1.5 mm. Requires an emissivity-corrected pyrometer: an uncorrected one is far outside the twin's 1-2 K reading budget, and source radiation alone is about 2 K.

sources.title: Strain engineering in GaN layers grown on silicon by molecular beam epitaxy: The critical role of growth temperature
sources.authors: Y. Cordier, N. Baron, S. Chenot, P. Vennegues, O. Tottereau et al. (CRHEA)
sources.source_locator: Sec. 2; Sec. 4; Fig. 2, 5; Sec. 5
sources.supports: CRHEA, Riber Compact 21 with NH3 and an Addon RF N50/63 plasma source. Plasma GaN at 700-720 C, 1.8 sccm, 400 W, Ga-rich, about 0.5 um/h: good layers with a flat growth front, but threading dislocations turn vertical and are filtered less, so the density exceeds 1e10 cm^-2; the lower temperature keeps more compressive stress (convex bow). sources.title: Determination of the atomic nitrogen flux from a radio frequency plasma nitride source for molecular beam epitaxy systems
sources.authors: F. Voulot, C. McCullough, P. Thompson, A. Burns, J. Geddes et al.
sources.publication: Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A 16, 3434-3437
sources.source_locator: Sec. II-IV; Eq. 1-3; Fig. 2-3
sources.supports: SVTA RF 4.5 (PBN tube 16.8 mm, single 2.8 mm aperture), modulated-beam QMS and gas throughput: dissociation fraction (= atom fraction of the fed N, i.e. eta at the source exit) 0.40 at 0.07 Torr source pressure falling to about 0.10 at 0.50 Torr (500 W); atom flux 0.45-0.85e18 s^-1, maximum at 0.32 Torr. At 0.1 and 0.2 Torr D rises with power to 0.30 and 0.26 at 500 W. From F = 3.22e19 x 2 D Q, D 0.40 at the low end corresponds to roughly 1-2 sccm; the high-pressure end is several sccm.
sources.does_not_support: Multi-hole aperture plates or UNI-Bulb sources; the delivered atom flux at the wafer (wall losses downstream).
sources.use: Evidence that eta at the source exit is at most about 0.4 and falls with source (bulb) pressure: eta = 1 (the B-p scenario) is not supported; a high-conductance plate that keeps the bulb pressure low (the B-L design idea) is the way to keep eta up at high flow.
